Jonah closed his empty right hand and let it hang by his side. He didn’t look away. He held his arm steady so her fingers could reach without bending toward him.

Mara walked around Jonah to face him on the next step down. She rested her left hand on the open palm he had offered.

Jonah breathed out through his nose as though this was easier than words. Mara let her breath match his. She watched his mouth for words when they were both still. He didn’t offer any. His shoulders relaxed.

Mara cupped his hand. A breath held in her throat. Her eyes fell to Jonah’s lips but he stayed still, waiting for her. The pressure of his hand was a question.

When she raised her eyes, his brows lowered as though he wanted to give her something she couldn’t name. She met his eyes and pulled her left hand into her coat pocket without letting go. He waited for what came next.

Mara slid her right hand into Jonah’s coat pocket without asking. His pocket held nothing but air and the lining. The soft cotton rustled lightly.

Jonah’s mouth softened at the edges as if a quiet smile was almost there.

Mara put her right arm around Jonah’s waist and drew his body in. The pocket lining slid smoothly as his breath caught in his throat.

They stood like this until Jonah slid his left hand into her jacket and Mara tilted her head to meet his lips.

“Wait.” Mara backed away from the kiss but not from Jonah’s body. They were still close enough that when he spoke, her face felt the small puffs of his breath.

“What would you have me do?” He released her hand from inside her jacket.

Mara turned into Jonah’s embrace. “Kiss me.” Her right hand returned to his coat pocket.

segment:
“Is anything wrong?” The voice was calm but didn’t ask more.

She shook her head. They walked in easy silence.

His hand on hers made it easy to walk without watching her feet. His posture let her read his breath without touching. The steady flow between them gave her confidence but never interrupted her thoughts. It felt as natural as air or walking, like the world was working as it should.

This is good. This is right.

Jonah took his hand back while Mara was looking at a tree. It smelled dry in the darkness. Her fingers moved for the contact that had gone away. Jonah took her left hand again.

“What do you think?” he said. He wasn’t sure she could hear him, but Mara knew what he meant. She’d heard it in his walk, the way his feet met the sidewalk and moved apart, as if he’d just lifted a weight and put it down. It wasn’t as if they walked separately; they were walking together. But not always the same pace. They matched and unmatched each other, like breath.

She let him speak. The thought was familiar, like a sound she remembered making. She looked straight ahead, so he might think she’d stopped listening.

“I think what we saw tonight was what happens when people focus on how they want to look and forget who they really are.” Her voice didn’t change, as if it had nothing to do with her body or her thoughts. “It’s like there’s a point where you lose the real person and can’t find your way back.”

His hand shifted slightly in hers. He was waiting, like he might have something to say if she was finished.

Mara looked down, watching her breath in the darkness. Her face relaxed and her shoulders loosened. The smell of wood and wet moss shifted with the wind. She watched his hand move toward her wrist as if it might not go there. The fingers didn’t squeeze but left a mark on her skin.

“What was that like?” he said, and she didn’t have to see his face to know what he meant. “When you lost yourself.”

His voice never changed pace. It kept the same distance and pitch as if it had nothing to do with the question. It was the kind of question only someone else could ask, something she couldn’t notice about herself. It was the difference between “What would it be like?” and “What happened?” Something that was always happening instead of happening once.

Jonah looked at her face, as if he wanted her to tell him how it felt. As if it mattered that she could feel it without saying.

segment:
They stood holding hands while he waited for what she chose next.

After a moment she shifted weight from one foot to the other and turned a quarter toward his truck. He met her gaze as he released her hand and bent for his keys from the front step, then stood again with his open palm waiting.

Mara folded her arms across her chest. Jonah reached for the truck door, pulled it open, and stepped away as he held the door with both hands to let her in. She climbed up. He closed the door and waited beside it.

When Mara lowered the passenger window, his head turned to put the truck’s hood between them. Her open hand stayed at the corner of the rolled-down window. His hand rested on top of her forearm where she held it out. After a moment she withdrew it and his hand fell back against his thigh.

Mara rolled up her window.

Jonah waited by the door, his face still turned away. She looked through the windshield. They’d stayed until almost eleven in a session that started at noon. How much time was left to the walk home?

She heard a small exhalation from beside her and his face returned to the driver side window. He stepped back, his hands away from the door. Mara climbed out and let the door shut by itself. Jonah stood still with his open hand waiting again. She took it and looked into his eyes.

After a moment she took his wrist in both of hers and lifted her voice so he could hear it under his engine. “I’ll walk.”

Jonah closed the driver-side window with one hand while he held hers and then turned to her with his eyes. Mara saw a question behind them.

“I can walk,” she said in a clearer voice. “I’ve done it before.” She let go of him and stood with her arms at her sides. He stopped holding her hand, straightened up, and stepped back.

Mara waited beside him and took a deep breath when Jonah opened the truck door with his eyes on hers. He pulled himself up and closed the door.

She watched the taillights shrink as the truck pulled out of Fulcrum’s driveway. She started walking.

He turned the truck onto the road that ran parallel to the creek between the town and the campus. Mara waited beside the gate to the campus and watched his taillights rise and fall as he passed the curve at the bridge.

The sky over the forest was clear and still. A breeze came off the water and cooled the air on her neck. Jonah’s truck stopped in front of the road that ran between his cabin and Mara’s. She watched his taillights reverse and come back to the campus gate. When he stepped out of the truck his headlights went off and his silhouette appeared beside the open door.

segment:
Mara let go a quiet exhale of her own and put her right hand in his left. His fingers closed round hers at the same time she gripped his, so softly the touch felt like a double shadow on her palms.

“Want to walk tonight?” The voice had that deep, easy tone when he spoke quietly.

“Yes.”

He walked with the same weight-and-pause rhythm that matched hers at first without thinking. She took the slow pace for granted but noticed the balance anyway. His steps never jostled hers.

Mara turned her head and breathed the night air. She tried to ignore the smell of sweat still clinging to her hair, the stiffness in her shoulders. She’d hated that session. The whole thing had been a terrible idea.

“You don’t like it either?” He walked at her elbow, his left hand still linked with hers, right hand swinging with the step.

“No.” Mara wanted to talk about the session; she wanted to stop thinking about it. “I never do when they’re in a pack like that. I want to help one, but—” She stopped, remembering how much her hand had slipped.

Jonah squeezed her fingers without shifting their grip and kept walking.

They walked across the street under the big fir tree and down the hill away from the parking lot. Mara let it get dark enough she couldn’t see the cars. They turned into the alley between the bank and the warehouse and walked out of sight of the road.

“We’re alone,” he said quietly.

Mara was too far from the cars to worry about their headlights. She felt the last tension leave her shoulders as they entered the empty alley. Jonah let go her left hand so they could swing into a new stride. She waited until the streetlights were behind them and turned to look at his eyes.

His eyes met hers before she found them. His body moved with her turn, his eyes shifted with her focus, his breath relaxed in a quiet sigh when they met. Mara let their gaze settle and waited as his eyes softened under hers and his lids widened so she could see his pupils widen too.

“Is this better?” he asked softly.

Mara let her mouth curve. “Yes.” She felt her muscles loosen with the grin. “Thanks.”

He smiled at her, his body loose and relaxed. The alley’s night smell of earth and wet leaves surrounded them as they walked together.

“I don’t know what I’d do without you there,” she said softly, turning her head to meet his eyes. “You save me so much time.”

She hadn’t meant that to be flirtation, but he grinned when he heard it. “I’ve been thinking about how I’d like to kiss you,” he said, his eyes bright in the dark.

Mara felt heat creep up her chest. “You really want to?”

segment:
A full breath took too much attention so Mara looked at their feet and moved hers under the truck’s bumper. Jonah put his right hand behind him on the step above and waited for her to move.

She tried a small step off the front porch. He let their joined hands stay steady without pushing against her. When she said, “Okay,” they walked.

Jonah took a wider step, moving her hand with the easy strength of his stride. After three steps Mara let the heel of her free hand rest on his elbow. She was used to holding someone when they walked. Jonah’s arm wasn’t tight, and he let her use his elbow without changing his pace or direction.

The walk took Mara through a part of herself she kept closed in the lab. When Jonah turned to look at her she let her hand slide higher on his sleeve to let them see each other more clearly. She watched his eyes follow the change. He said nothing while she moved her hand to rest between his arm and side.

When he looked forward again he took a wider step, then slowed his pace so Mara could move next to him. When she said nothing for a long time Jonah finally asked, “Why did you do it?”

“Do what?”

Jonah glanced over so the question was more of a look. “Stop them.”

“Why not? They’re hurting people. I won’t let people I care about get hurt.”

He didn’t argue with her. They reached the sidewalk in the street and Mara let her left hand fall from his to her side. She stood alone while Jonah unlocked the truck door, then watched as he put his keys on the front seat and shut the door again. When he turned to face her she knew exactly what he was going to ask.

“Can I offer you a ride?” The voice was steady.

“I’ll walk, thanks. I can walk to my own apartment.”

Mara didn’t expect an argument and didn’t get one. After two steps Mara said, “Can we just walk for a while? Can we be alone?”

He turned so they could meet his eyes. She waited to see what he would say.

“Yes.”

She took his offered hand and he let them walk slowly. After four steps she said, “I want to stop for a moment and put my forehead against yours so we can just breathe together.”

He stopped at the corner and turned to face her, then closed one eye. Mara moved to him and lifted their joined hands to his chest to stand steady. Jonah kept his voice low. “I’m breathing for both of us right now.”

Mara put her forehead against his while Jonah’s other hand went slowly to hold her arm. She was quiet until she heard the distant sound of traffic, then finally looked up. “What about a kiss?”

“If you want one.”
